rounds.fact: Blizzard's late-90s site supported both Diablo and StarCraft, two games that helped define entire genres and whose online play features were unusually ambitious for their time.
Xanga combined blogging with heavy profile customization and briefly rivaled MySpace in popularity among teens before losing ground in the mid-2000s.
Airbnb started in 2008 with the founders renting out air mattresses in their own apartment during a design conference, which is where the original name came from.
Addicting Games grew rapidly during the mid-2000s Flash gaming boom, hosting thousands of free browser games at a time when installing a game usually still meant buying a physical disc.
Digital Trends grew as a general consumer-electronics review site during the mid-2000s, competing for readers alongside CNET and Engadget in a crowded gadget-blog era.
